sentences.text: Hsisosuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliform that lived in China as a medium-sized predator reaching about 3 meters in length.
The genus Hsisosuchus was described by Young and Chow in 1953, with the authority for the name recorded as Young & Chow, 1953.

Fossils of the species H. chungkingensis were discovered in the Shangshaximiao Formation near Chongqing city, while H. dashanpuensis was found in the Xiashaximiao Formation and H. chowi was found in the Shangshaximiao Formation.
The holotype of H. chowi includes a nearly complete skull measuring 25 cm long, along with mandibles, most of the vertebral column, and many other skeletal parts.
Hsisosuchus is classified within the family Hsisosuchidae, though the Paleobiology Database classifies it as belonging to the parent group Shartegosuchidae.
Hsisosuchus fossils date to the Middle and Late Jurassic periods, living between the Bajocian and Tithonian stages, approximately 170.9 to 143.1 million years ago.
